items.title: Tether lands first Big Four audit as KPMG signs off on 2025 statements
points: KPMG issued an unqualified audit opinion (auditors found no material problems with how the financial statements are presented) on Tether's 2025 financials.
Ends years of scrutiny over reserve disclosures for USDT, the world's most widely used stablecoin (a crypto token pegged 1:1 to a currency like the US dollar).
Comes after an $18.5 million 2021 New York settlement and a $41 million 2022 CFTC fine over false claims that USDT was fully backed.
CEO Paolo Ardoino called it Tether's 'largest inaugural financial audit'; the opinion is not an endorsement of the business or a guarantee Tether can meet obligations.

items.title: SEC shelves crypto rule meeting with no new date
points: The SEC postponed a planned crypto rulemaking meeting citing an unforeseen scheduling issue, with no replacement date announced.
The delay follows Senate Democrats pushing back the Clarity Act, the crypto market-structure bill.

items.title: Bitcoin Red Team uses Chinese AI to hunt code flaws
points: Red Team member Calle says Chinese models including Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 are finding bugs in Bitcoin's open-source codebase faster than expected.
A 'red team' is a group that deliberately attacks a system to uncover vulnerabilities before malicious actors do.

items.title: Anthropic quietly watermarks all Claude outputs
points: Anthropic's newest Claude models embed invisible, machine-readable watermarks (hidden signals in text that software can detect) into every output to flag AI-generated content.
Implementation details have not been disclosed publicly.

items.title: Polymarket's POLY token launch slips
points: Polymarket's CMO said in October 2025 that a POLY token would launch with 5–10% of supply reserved for retroactive user airdrops.
The platform relaunched in the US in May 2026 — a stated prerequisite for the token generation event — but no launch date has followed.
Polymarket traders put 60% odds the token does not launch before 2027; Q4 2026 is the single most likely quarter at 20%.
The firm revamped its marketing team and expanded US hiring last week ahead of fall events.

items.title: Citi CEO Jane Fraser backs the CLARITY Act
points: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser publicly endorsed the CLARITY Act, the bill defining which regulator oversees which digital assets (splitting jurisdiction between the SEC and CFTC).
Fraser said Citi wants passage of 'a good bill,' signaling banks prefer regulatory certainty over today's fragmented oversight.
The endorsement marks major traditional-finance alignment with crypto market structure reform rather than opposition to it.

issues.subject: Citi CEO Wants the CLARITY Act Passed

headlines: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser publicly endorsed the CLARITY Act, signaling major bank support for comprehensive cryptocurrency market structure regulation as Congress debates the legislation.
The CLARITY Act aims to establish clearer regulatory jurisdiction and oversight frameworks for digital assets, with backing from traditional finance institutions seeking defined rules.
Fraser indicated Citi wants passage of "a good bill," suggesting banking sector preference for regulatory certainty over the current fragmented crypto oversight landscape.

sections.title: Citi's Position on CLARITY Act
points: 1. Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser stated the bank supports passage of the CLARITY Act during discussions about crypto market structure reform.
2. Fraser's comment signals that major traditional financial institutions view comprehensive digital asset regulation as preferable to existing ambiguity.
3. The endorsement indicates banking sector alignment with establishing clear regulatory frameworks rather than blocking crypto market development.
